title: SE hands-on lab script and scorer (draft)
body:
Purpose:
A compact, repeatable 20–30 minute hands-on lab script that Sales Engineers (SEs) can run with prospect platform teams during pilots or technical discovery. Includes a simple scoring rubric to quantify readiness and signal fit for: Dedicated, Hosted, or Private deployment pathways.

Audience:
- Primary: Platform/Infrastructure engineers, integration architects
- Secondary: Product managers, SRE leads, security reviewers (observe-only)

Outcomes (what SE should achieve by end of session):
1) Validate three technical constraints quickly: peak throughput requirement, latency SLO, data locality/compliance need.
2) Demonstrate a concrete fallback or routing policy example in the Redwood Console (mock or live demo).
3) Elicit commercial signals (willingness to commit reserved capacity; KMS/HSM needs).
4) Produce a single-line recommendation and a score (0–12) to hand to AE.

Prep (before session) - checklist for SE:
- Confirm access: prospect has small sandbox cluster or a pre-provisioned test dataset (if not, use synthetic dataset).
- Create a quick model selection: pick one lower-latency and one cost-efficient model variant from the catalog.
- Pre-load two short prompt templates that reflect the prospect workload.
- Create a Console view with a routing policy example (or a recorded GIF).
- Save scoring sheet in CRM note template.

Session flow (20–30 mins)
1) 0:00–02:00 — Quick framing (SE)
- 90s introduction: explain goal = validate constraints, demo two guardrails, decide next best demo.
- Set expectations: this is exploratory, we’ll score fit factors at the end.

2) 02:00–10:00 — Rapid workload probe (interactive)
- Ask prospect to describe their core call pattern (short example): tokens per request, typical concurrency, and 99th percentile latency requirement.
- SE runs two short prompts (provided) against the chosen model variants (live or recorded).
- Capture observed latency, token counts, and any output-quality notes.
- If live: show Console route selection and explain fallback to cheaper variant. If recorded: narrate the same steps and show GIF.

3) 10:00–18:00 — Failure and fallback walkthrough (roleplay)
- Trigger a simulated capacity constraint: show how Smart Routing can route to a compatible variant or region.
- Walk through an autoscale policy example for Dedicated pools and show cost implications (quick chart).
- Ask prospect: what’s the acceptable degradation? (lossy answers ok)

4) 18:00–25:00 — Security & compliance quick check
- Confirm data residency requirements and any KMS/HSM needs.
- Quick callout: Private deployment tradeoffs (on‑prem) vs Private VPC—time to delivery.
- Surface audit/logging asks and whether they need archived telemetry retention.

5) 25:00–30:00 — Wrap & score
- Run through the scoring rubric.
- Outcome: 1-sentence recommendation + score + top 2 follow-ups (technical & commercial).

Scoring rubric (0–4 per pillar, total 0–12) — use integer ticks only.
- Pillar A — Latency & SLA fit (0: not suitable / 4: comfortably within SLO)
  - 4 = <50ms median demo latency with low variance AND 99th percentile within target
  - 2 = median close but 99th misses occasionally
  - 0 = median significantly above target
- Pillar B — Throughput & Capacity fit (0: major mismatch / 4: clear fit)
  - 4 = expected concurrency and burst patterns fit Dedicated or Hosted autoscale ranges
  - 2 = borderline; may need burst reservations or batching changes
  - 0 = requires large capacity redesign or custom infra
- Pillar C — Security & Deployment constraints (0: blocker / 4: ready)
  - 4 = no special keys/HSM needs; VPC fit; legal team likely OK
  - 2 = needs KMS integration or stricter audit retention but feasible
  - 0 = requires full on‑prem air‑gapped solution or non-negotiable controls

Scoring guidance: 9–12 = high-fit (recommend pilot with reserved capacity option); 5–8 = moderate-fit (pilot with technical scope and canary controls); 0–4 = low-fit (introduce Private or professional services involvement).

AE handoff template (paste into CRM as final note):
- One-line recommendation: [High/Moderate/Low] fit — [short rationale].
- Score: X/12.
- Top technical follow-ups (2): e.g., KMS integration, bench test for QPS at 95th pctl.
- Commercial signals: budget window, procurement timeline, preferred deployment mode.
- Attach: console-snapshot.png; demo-gif.mp4 (if recorded)

Objection playbook (quick snippets for SE)
- "We can’t tolerate any drift in model outputs": Suggest -- a pilot with Redwood Optimize enabled + eval set that runs nightly; propose quality regression alerting.
- "Cost seems unpredictable": Show microbatching + prefix caching example that reduced per‑token costs 20–35% in similar workload (share anonymized metric).
- "We need HSM-backed keys": Note Private deployment + KMS/HSM option; outline typical 8–12 week delivery for on‑prem package vs 4–6 weeks for VPC with dedicated KMS.

Training notes for SEs (internal)
- Use the rubric as a conversation guide not a checklist — capture nuance in the CRM narrative.
- If using a recorded demo, annotate timestamps for 1) latency demo 2) fallback flow 3) routing policy.
- When in doubt, mark security pillar conservative (lower score) — handoff to Solutions Eng for escalation.

Follow-ups (post-session playbook)
- Within 24 hours: SE uploads annotated demo + scoring sheet to CRM and pings AE + Solutions Eng.
- If score >=9: AE to propose reserved capacity POC + Procurement introduction.
- If 5–8: schedule 60–90 minute deep technical bench with infra SREs.
- If <5: propose architecture review and PS estimate.

Appendix: quick paste-ready prompts (two)
- Prompt A (short form): "Summarize the following user message in 25 tokens: [sample user text]"
- Prompt B (compositional): "Given knowledge base excerpt X and user query Y, produce a 3‑line answer and cite source lines."

Notes-to-self (SE quick hacks)
- If prospect uses large context windows frequently, pre-select quantized model variant to demo cold-start speed.
- Keep one pre-made cost comparison slide per deployment mode in your slide deck.

End of doc.
